title: Entity span audit: trim, snap, score
scenario: Clean sloppy character-range NER selections (trim whitespace, resolve label aliases, snap to token boundaries, dedupe), export spans for non-gold documents and score each annotator against adjudicated gold spans with exact-match P/R/F1 plus a label-confusion table.

verified.why_correct: finditer's m.end() is already end-exclusive, matching the span convention, and the pattern keeps inner apostrophes (O'Brien) and splits punctuation into single tokens exactly as the README describes.

The arithmetic looks backwards, but lstrip measures the leading whitespace (added to start) and rstrip the trailing whitespace (subtracted from end). An all-whitespace selection makes start >= end and is rejected as empty.

bugs.title: Snap covers the token that starts at the span end
bugs.old: covered = [t for t in tokens if t.start < end and t.end > start]
bugs.new: covered = [t for t in tokens if t.start <= end and t.end > start]
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_exported_spans: four spans grow by one character to swallow the following punctuation: 'Redwood Media,' (25, 39), 'Dublin.' (52, 59), 'Global Freight Inc.' (0, 19) and 'Milan.' (53, 59). Spans followed by a space are unchanged.
bugs.why: With end-exclusive offsets, a token that starts exactly at `end` shares no character with the span. `<=` pulls in a punctuation mark that directly follows the entity ("Redwood Media,", "Dublin."), widening the span by one. Words followed by a space are unaffected, which is why only some spans move.
hints: Which exported spans changed, and what character follows each of them in the text?
Look at how snap decides whether a token is covered by the selection.
In snap, `t.start <= end` should be `t.start < end` (end is exclusive).
probes: Why did "Liam O'Brien" and "Hannah Becker" keep their offsets while "Milan" moved?
Why don't the gold-document scores change with this slip, even though snapping runs on every span?

bugs.title: Non-gold spans scored as false positives
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_annotator_scores: ann-a shows fp 4 / precision 0.636 / f1 0.7 (expected fp 1, 0.875, 0.824), ann-b fp 7 / precision 0.364 / f1 0.32, and an extra ann-d row with tp 0, fp 3 and all metrics 0.0. tp, fn and recall are unchanged.
bugs.why: `scored` is the gold-document subset, but the loop walks every accepted span. Spans on documents with no gold become false positives, and ann-d, who only annotated non-gold documents, gets a row with tp 0.
hints: Where does ann-d's row come from? Which documents did ann-d annotate?
Compare the list score_annotators builds with the list it actually iterates over.
Loop over `scored`, not `spans`, when filling predicted/docs_seen.
probes: Why did tp and fn stay the same for ann-a while fp grew?
Why is the confusion table unaffected even though it also reads every span?

bugs.title: Confusion ties left in insertion order
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_label_confusions: [['ORG', 'LOC', 2], ['LOC', 'ORG', 2], ['PERSON', 'ORG', 1]]; the two count-2 rows are swapped.
bugs.why: most_common() orders by count only and keeps first-seen order among equal counts. ann-a's ORG→LOC confusion comes first in the file, so it is listed before LOC→ORG instead of after it alphabetically.
hints: The counts are right; only the order of two rows differs. What do those rows have in common?
Look at how rank_confusions orders the Counter.
Replace most_common() with sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])).
probes: What order does Counter.most_common use for equal counts, and why is that fragile?
If ann-b's rows came first in the CSV, would the test have passed with the old code?

context_qa.q: What does build_report do, step by step?
context_qa.a: It loads documents, label aliases and gold spans, reads the annotation rows, then calls `spans.normalize_all` to clean them into `Span` objects plus a Counter of rejection reasons. It then builds the export (non-gold docs), accepted counts, `scoring.score_annotators`, the ranked confusions and the gold label counts.

context_qa.q: How is a single annotation row turned into a Span?
context_qa.a: `Normalizer.normalize` looks up the document, resolves the label via `resolve_label`, parses both offsets, checks `0 <= start < end <= len(text)`, calls `trim_whitespace`, then `tokens.snap` with the cached tokens for that document. Any `SpanError` raised along the way carries the rejection reason.

context_qa.q: What does tokenize return for "Dr. Kenji"?
context_qa.a: Three `Token` objects: `Dr` (0, 2), `.` (2, 3) and `Kenji` (4, 9). The end offsets come straight from `re.finditer`.
`normalize_all` keeps a set of accepted `Span` dataclass instances (frozen, so hashable). A cleaned span equal to one already in the set increments `rejected["duplicate"]` and is not added.

context_qa.q: What is in the gold list and how is it keyed?
context_qa.a: `read_gold` returns tuples `(doc_id, start, end, LABEL)`. `score_annotators` uses them as a set, and `confusion_counts` builds a dict keyed by `(doc_id, start, end)` mapping to the gold label.

context_qa.q: Which annotators appear in the scores table?
context_qa.a: One row for each annotator key in `predicted`, sorted by id. `predicted` is filled inside `score_annotators` from the spans its loop iterates over.
`export_spans` sorts all spans by `(doc_id, start, end, annotator)`, skips gold documents, and groups the rest per doc id with the text slice `docs[doc_id][start:end]`.
